title: Billing Automation Readiness Diagnostic
subtitle: A 5-section diagnostic to confirm your billing automation project is ready to build before you spend $50,000 finding out it isn't

sections.title: Pricing Structure Clarity
sections.description: Confirm every pricing scenario is documented before anyone writes code.

items.text: List every pricing tier you use (transfer, renewal, new, custom) in under 60 seconds without checking a spreadsheet
items.tip: If you need to ask someone else, your pricing isn't documented yet.

items.text: Document the markup or discount rule for every pricing tier in writing
items.tip: Any rule that lives in someone's head will become a 2-week delay during build.

items.text: Quantify exactly how many customers have custom pricing outside standard tiers
items.tip: If the answer is 'a few' or 'not sure,' run a query before scoping.

items.text: Confirm the person who knows pricing exceptions is available for the full project duration
items.tip: If they're on leave or leaving the company, pause and document first.

sections.title: Data Source Readiness
sections.description: Verify the source of truth exists, is accessible, and is accurate.

items.text: Identify a single source of truth for usage and customer data with API or export access
items.tip: If data lives in 3 systems with no master, fix that before automating.

items.text: Spot-check 20 recent records to confirm the data matches what gets invoiced today
items.tip: Manual cleanup happening in spreadsheets is hidden scope you must surface now.

items.text: Verify API credentials, rate limits, and authentication method for every source system
items.tip: Budget 1 week for procurement if credentials don't exist yet.

sections.title: Exception Handling
sections.description: Surface the edge cases that blow up timelines.

items.text: Write down every billing edge case from the last 6 months with how it was resolved
items.tip: Pull 6 months of invoice adjustments from accounting to find them.

items.text: Define rounding, proration, and partial-month rules in writing
items.tip: These cause more revisions than any other category.

items.text: Set a dollar threshold above which invoices route to manual review
items.tip: A $500 threshold prevents 90% of automation disasters in the first 3 months.

sections.title: Integration Requirements
sections.description: Confirm where data needs to go and how.

items.text: Map the exact destination system (Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite) and required invoice fields
items.tip: Export a sample invoice and label every field's source.

items.text: Confirm how invoices reach customers (email, portal, PDF attachment) and who triggers send
items.tip: Auto-send vs review-then-send is a 40-hour build difference.

items.text: Plan how the system handles API failures, duplicates, and partial syncs
items.tip: Decide retry logic and alert recipients before the build starts.

sections.title: Validation & Approval Process
sections.description: Define who checks what before invoices go out.

items.text: Name the single person who approves invoice batches before they send
items.tip: Committees create bottlenecks; one named approver ships invoices on time.

items.text: Define the 3 to 5 QA checks that must pass before an invoice batch is approved
items.tip: Examples: totals match usage data, customer count matches active accounts, no $0 invoices.

items.text: Document the rollback procedure if a bad invoice batch ships to customers
items.tip: Know in advance who issues credits and how customers are notified.

items.text: Schedule a 30-minute review at week 1, week 2, and week 4 after launch
items.tip: Most automation errors surface in the first billing cycle; catch them before month 2.

completion_cta.headline: You finished the diagnostic. Now what?
completion_cta.description: If you answered every item in under 2 minutes, you're ready to scope a billing automation project. If you flagged 3 or more items, do the homework first; that homework saves you 6 figures and 4 months. Either way, you just avoided the most expensive mistake in billing automation: starting before you were ready.
